about: One ladder per recipient, bottom rung first: every route the law and the body's own policies allow, in the order a slow, complete, worst-case process takes them. Every rung is insisted on, whatever the body tells us our options are. Top of the ladder: full disclosure.
rights: Disclosure received at any stage is accepted without prejudice and is not accepted as settlement of any question of earlier concealment; all rights are reserved.

markers.chestnut: Old chestnut: not held, out of scope, refused, sent elsewhere, or found later
markers.policy: Pointed to its own policy ("if you are not satisfied ...")

method: Replies read from the case mail (automatic receipts left out); each reply checked against the pattern set in the Dartboard autoresearch log; ladders from UK statute, procedure rules and each body's published policy, checked 2 Nov 2026.

preserve.name: Preserve + reserve rights
preserve.clock: Send before or with the first request, then restate at every rung
preserve.trig: Sent: climb to the first request
preserve.cite: FOIA s.77 and EIR reg 19 (altering or concealing a requested record is an offence); Limitation Act 1980 s.32
preserve.makes: A dated notice that the records matter, so any later loss needs an explanation

enquiry.name: Ask what is published
enquiry.trig: Nothing found, or no answer: make the statutory request
enquiry.cite: Their publication scheme (FOIA s.19) and catalogue
enquiry.makes: Catalogue references and file titles to quote

register.name: Statutory registers
register.clock: Register open to inspection; no reply clock
register.trig: Entry missing or thin: request the file behind it
register.cite: The statute that keeps the register

charity.name: Charity route
charity.makes: A trustee answer or a regulator file

foi.name: Information request
foi.clock: 20 working days (FOIA s.10(1)); longer only with a written public-interest notice (s.17(2))
foi.trig: Day 21 with no answer, or any refusal, "not held" or part answer: ask for internal review
foi.cite: FOIA s.1(1) (confirm and communicate), s.16 (advice and assistance), s.17 (refusal must name the exemption and why)
foi.makes: A dated answer, or a dated failure to answer

eir.name: Environmental information
eir.clock: 20 working days (EIR reg 5(2)); 40 only if complex and notified (reg 7)
eir.trig: Late, refused or "not held": ask for reconsideration under reg 11
eir.cite: EIR reg 5 (duty to make available), reg 9 (advice), reg 12(4)(a) (not held must be shown), reg 12(5) (public-interest test)
eir.makes: A dated answer under the stricter environmental regime (no cost limit)

sar.name: Personal data
sar.clock: One calendar month (UK GDPR Art 12(3)); two more months only if complex and notified in the first month
sar.trig: Late or incomplete: complaint to the controller, then to the Information Commission (DPA 2018 s.165)
sar.cite: UK GDPR Art 15; DPA 2018 s.45 (law-enforcement data)
sar.makes: Your own data, or a dated failure

review.name: Internal review
review.clock: FOIA: ask within 40 working days; answer usually in 20, never over 40 (s.45 Code of Practice). EIR: ask within 40 working days; answer within 40 (reg 11)
review.who: A senior officer not involved first time
review.trig: No answer in time, or the refusal upheld: complain to the Information Commission (FOIA s.50)
review.cite: FOIA s.45 Code of Practice, part 5; EIR reg 11

complaint.name: Complaints procedure
complaint.who: Complaints team, then a senior manager
complaint.trig: Final answer, or no answer: ombudsman or independent reviewer
complaint.makes: A findings letter on how they handled it

icr.name: Independent reviewer
icr.clock: After the body's own two stages
icr.trig: ICR decision: Parliamentary Ombudsman through an MP

iopc.name: Police oversight
iopc.clock: Ours: ask for a review within 28 days of the outcome letter
iopc.who: IOPC or the Police and Crime Commissioner
iopc.makes: An independent review of the police handling

iac.name: Independent adjudicator
iac.clock: After the body's own complaints stages

ico.name: Information Commission
ico.clock: No fixed clock for the Commission. Ours: complain soon after the internal review answer (data protection: within 3 months of the last meaningful contact)
ico.trig: Decision notice: appeal to the First-tier Tribunal within 28 days
ico.cite: FOIA s.50; EIR reg 18; DPA 2018 s.165
ico.makes: A decision notice that binds the body

tribunal.name: Tribunal
tribunal.clock: Ours: 28 days from the decision notice (Tribunal Procedure Rules (GRC) r.22(1)(b))
tribunal.who: First-tier Tribunal (Information Rights), then the Upper Tribunal
tribunal.trig: Decision: Upper Tribunal on a point of law
tribunal.cite: FOIA s.57 and s.58; EIR reg 18; DPA 2018 s.166 (order to progress a complaint)
tribunal.makes: A judicial decision on the record

regulator.name: Professional regulator
regulator.trig: Outcome: tribunal or ombudsman of that profession

democratic.name: Elected members
democratic.trig: An MP referral is the only door to the Parliamentary Ombudsman
democratic.makes: A letter from the body to an elected member

psow.name: Ombudsman (Wales)
psow.clock: Ours: complain to the body first, then to the Ombudsman within one year of first notice (PSOW Act 2019 s.8(1)(c), s.9)
psow.trig: Report or refusal: judicial review only

phso.name: Ombudsman (UK)
phso.clock: Ours: through an MP, normally within 12 months of first notice (Parliamentary Commissioner Act 1967 s.6(3))
phso.trig: Report or refusal: judicial review only

offence.name: Concealment report
offence.clock: Summary offence: a time limit for prosecution runs from when the evidence is known
offence.trig: Only on evidence a record was altered, blocked, erased, destroyed or concealed after the request

preaction.name: Letter before claim
preaction.clock: Letter before claim: reply within 14 days (simple) to 3 months (complex) (Practice Direction Pre-Action Conduct para 6)
preaction.trig: No proper reply: issue, or apply for disclosure
preaction.cite: Practice Direction Pre-Action Conduct; Judicial Review Pre-Action Protocol

disclosure.name: Court disclosure
disclosure.trig: Order made: documents produced on oath
disclosure.cite: CPR 31.16, CPR 31.17; Norwich Pharmacal v Customs and Excise [1974] AC 133

advice.clock: With the request; answer within the 20 working days
advice.makes: Their own description of what they hold and how it is filed

notheld.clock: Raise in the review, then with the Commission
notheld.cite: EIR reg 12(4)(a) and FOIA s.1: "not held" is judged on the balance of probabilities, so ask what was searched, where, by whom and with which terms
notheld.makes: A search record that can be tested

searchq.clock: Raise in the review, then with the Commission
searchq.cite: EIR reg 12(4)(a) and FOIA s.1: "not held" is judged on the balance of probabilities, so ask what was searched, where, by whom and with which terms
searchq.makes: A search record that can be tested

records.clock: Ask with any request (20 working days)
records.cite: Code of Practice on records management (FOIA s.46); Public Records Act 1958 s.3 for public records
records.makes: The retention rule and the destruction record, or proof none exists

ut.clock: Ours: ask the First-tier Tribunal for permission within 28 days of its decision (GRC rules r.42), then the Upper Tribunal within 1 month
ut.cite: Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007 s.11
ut.makes: A binding ruling on the law

jr.clock: Ours: protocol letter, reply in 14 days; claim promptly and in any event within 3 months of the decision (CPR 54.5(1)); the parties cannot extend this (r.54.5(2))
jr.cite: Judicial Review Pre-Action Protocol; CPR Part 54
jr.makes: A ruling on whether the decision was lawful

lbc.cite: Practice Direction Pre-Action Conduct paras 6 and 13-16
lbc.makes: Their formal legal position, and costs consequences if they ignore it

dpa167.makes: An order to comply with the subject access request

cpr3116.clock: Court timetable; only against someone likely to be a party
cpr3116.makes: Documents before any claim is issued

icosar.clock: Ours: within 3 months of the last meaningful contact with the controller
icosar.makes: A Commission view on the subject access request
